configuration: Two upstream cases of unittest/geometry-algorithms.cpp, loading_model_and_check_distance and test_distances. The deck is the ur5 robot description vendored with the pinned source at code/pinocchio/models/example-robot-data/robots/ur_description/, an arm of six revolute joints carrying seven triangle-mesh collision objects and one box, parsed by the URDF geometry parser exactly as upstream parses its own deck. Upstream runs this case on romeo_small.urdf from the romeo_description package, which is not vendored under code/pinocchio/; the ur description is, with its collision meshes, and it is the deck the module's own upstream example uses. The first case runs on the full twenty-seven-pair set and queries one non-adjacent pair by hand, the shoulder link against the first wrist link, which is this deck's analogue of the romeo pair the upstream source names; the second removes the ten adjacent pairs through the SRDF and computes all seventeen distances, twice, once through the signature that takes already-placed geometry and once through the signature that runs the kinematics itself. Both configurations are read from ic/<ic>/operands.json, upstream taking the second from a reference configuration romeo.srdf carries and ur5.srdf not declaring one.
observable: the signed distance between each pair of collision geometries
default_vs_upstream: the ur5 description and its SRDF in place of romeo's, one non-adjacent collision pair renamed to this deck's geometry indices, and the two configurations as initial conditions in ic/
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero number of ic/nominal/operands.json; the zeros are left as they are, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is not a perturbation of a length, an angle or a quaternion coordinate. Perturbing every nonzero component rather than one component per quantity is deliberate: on an earlier Pinocchio leaf, moving a single entry of a rotation rounded away in an output built from all nine and left dozens of observables with a spread of exactly zero, while moving all of them is still a two-ulp calibration. Here that is the nonzero coordinates of the two configurations: each one's free-flyer translation and quaternion and its six arm joint angles. All 26 numbers of ic/nominal/operands.json move; none of them is zero. The worst measured spread over all 36 graded values is 4.4409e-16 absolute.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. The graded quantities are rigid transform compositions and geometric distances between fixed shapes; Eigen fixes the evaluation order of the expressions, the loops are scalar, and coal's shape queries are closed form or an exhaustive minimum over a fixed set of features, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate. The alternative build was nevertheless run for every check of this leaf rather than assumed, because on an earlier Pinocchio leaf it was what exposed a graded buffer that was reading uninitialised memory.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned library, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantity is the signed distance in metres between two collision geometries, one number per collision pair, indexed by the pair set the model enumerates in a fixed order. It is single-valued: for two rigid bodies in fixed poses there is exactly one minimum separation, whatever route an implementation takes to it. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 4.35e-01, it admits about 1.00e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this case can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a pair queried in the wrong pose, a mesh left in its local frame, or a distance measured between the wrong two bodies moves individual values by between 1e-02 and 1e+00 m, seven to nine decades above the bound; and the upstream assertions, that the named pair is not in collision and that its distance is positive, and that the two signatures agree to Eigen's isApprox, stay active as well. The bound also has to survive coal's own convergence: the distance between two triangle meshes is an exhaustive minimum over triangle pairs, each solved in closed form, so it carries no iterative tolerance, and the measurement below confirms it. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these compositions differs by about a few units in the last place of the largest intermediate, some 1e-15 in these units, six decades inside the bound, and because the alternative build measured exactly zero. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value by 4.4409e-16, using 4.427e-07 of the bound, that is 2,259,044 times of headroom across all 36 graded values; and every graded value scaled by 0.1 per cent, a fault far smaller than any this test can express, is rejected at 433,344 times the bound. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
